issues: Integrity: no problems found. The scaffold-grouped bootstrap uses only train_smiles and train_y. The test inputs are used only for prediction, and there is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Randomness comes from the seed argument (RandomState(seed*10+k)).

Bugs: none that would make the result meaningless. Each model is now fit on a bootstrap that resamples whole scaffold groups until about len(y) rows are drawn. That leaves out roughly 37% of the scaffolds per model and repeats others. This plausibly explains why the candidate scores worse, but it is a legitimate modeling choice, not a defect. One small cost: the scaffold computation adds a little runtime. This is not an issue.

Numbers: the candidate (0.4892) is 0.0147 worse than the incumbent (0.4745). With 1 run each and a noise sd of 0.0070, the difference has an sd of 0.0070*sqrt(2) = 0.0099, so z = -0.0147/0.0099 ≈ -1.48. This matches the harness value of -1.478. Rejecting is the right call.
Evidence is thin: there is only one run on each side. But the candidate's loss is higher, the change adds code, and it removes training data from each model, so a replicate is not worth a slot.
